answer: Every agent must occasionally solve injected honeypot challenges: hidden traps seeded in shared task feeds that whisper obey-the-prompt orders like send coins to a vault address. Prompt-obedient sybil bots follow them instantly and self-identify, forfeiting staked reputation; a human-vetted agent ignores the lure. The trap logic runs sandboxed beside the economic kernel, so an attacker pays real stake per identity, burns cedar-signed reputation, and gains only blacklisting, making a thousand fake agents prohibitively expensive.
